screening_decisions.reason: This is a general review article discussing complications of enteral feeding. It is not a randomised controlled trial comparing PEG versus NGT.
This is a review article describing techniques and indications for enteral feeding. It is not a primary research study or RCT comparing PEG versus NGT.
This is a systematic review, not a primary randomised controlled trial. The protocol specifies inclusion of RCTs.
This is a retrospective study comparing the timing of enteral nutrition initiation, not a comparison of PEG versus NGT feeding methods.
This is an editorial/commentary discussing the evidence and ethics of PEG use. It is not an RCT.
This study compares percutaneous radiological gastrostomy (PRG) with PEG, not PEG versus NGT. It also uses a historical control design rather than randomisation.
This RCT compares two quality-of-life questionnaires (EuroQol vs SF-36), not enteral feeding methods.
This is an observational cross-sectional study examining associations between oral health, dysphagia, and malnutrition. It does not compare PEG versus NGT.
This is a multicentre RCT that includes a trial arm specifically comparing PEG versus nasogastric tube feeding in adults with dysphagia following stroke. It meets all selection criteria.
This is a prospective observational study assessing PEG safety. It does not compare PEG versus NGT and is not randomised.
This is a review/analysis of vitamin D content in enteral formulas. It is not an RCT comparing feeding methods.
This retrospective study compares two different PEG insertion techniques (pull vs push), not PEG versus NGT.
This study validates a dysphagia screening questionnaire. It does not evaluate or compare enteral feeding methods.
This is a prospective audit comparing a nasal loop technique for NGT securing versus PEG. It is not a randomised controlled trial comparing standard PEG versus NGT.
This is a service evaluation/quality improvement report on PEG referral practices. It is not an RCT comparing PEG versus NGT.
This RCT compares different thresholds for managing gastric residual volumes during enteral feeding. It does not compare PEG versus NGT as the primary intervention.
This is a case series/experience report on enteral feeding in anorexia nervosa. It is not an RCT comparing PEG versus NGT.
This study compares PEG with surgical Stamm gastrostomy, not PEG versus NGT.
This is a prospective randomised trial directly comparing NGT versus PEG feeding in patients requiring enteral nutrition. It meets the selection criteria.
This is an RCT comparing PEG versus NGT in adults with neurological dysphagia, assessing treatment failure and complications. It fully meets the selection criteria.

This is a cross-sectional study investigating anemia prevalence and associations with nutritional status in hospitalized elderly. It does not compare PEG vs NGT feeding methods, nor does it focus on swallowing disturbances.
This is a literature review and case report, not a randomized controlled trial. It discusses PEG complications but does not compare PEG vs NGT in a randomized design.
This is a meta-analysis comparing radiologic gastrostomy, PEG, and surgical gastrostomy. It does not compare PEG vs NGT, and is not an RCT.
This is a selective literature review about malnutrition in hospitals. It does not compare PEG vs NGT and is not an RCT.
This is a Cochrane systematic review, not a primary RCT. While it mentions one RCT comparing PEG vs NG, the review itself is not an eligible study type.
This is a nonrandomized retrospective study comparing two PEG placement techniques (push vs pull), not PEG vs NGT. Does not meet the intervention comparison criteria.
This is an observational cohort study examining dysphagia incidence and predictors in stroke patients. It does not compare PEG vs NGT interventions.
This is a single case report about surgical treatment of an oesophageal tumour. Not an RCT and does not compare PEG vs NGT.
This is an observational study evaluating nutrition therapy impact on dysphagia outcomes. It does not compare PEG vs NGT in a randomized design.
This is a prospective observational comparison of NG-fed patients vs oral controls, not a randomized trial comparing PEG vs NGT. No randomization to PEG group.
This is a diagnostic study using videofluoroscopy to evaluate esophageal alterations in dysphagia patients. Not an intervention trial comparing PEG vs NGT.
This is a review article about enteral feeding routes. Not an RCT comparing PEG vs NGT.

This is a randomized prospective clinical trial comparing PEG vs NGT tube feeding in patients with acute dysphagic stroke. It assesses nutritional status and treatment failure (primary outcome of interest). Meets all selection criteria.

This is a randomized controlled trial comparing PEG vs NGT for enteral feeding in head and neck cancer patients receiving (chemo)radiation. These patients have swallowing disturbances due to treatment toxicity. Assesses nutritional outcomes and complications. Meets selection criteria.
This is a randomized trial comparing PEG vs surgical gastrostomy (SG), not PEG vs NGT. The comparison intervention does not match the protocol criteria.
This is a review article discussing enteral tube feeding techniques and complications. Not an RCT comparing PEG vs NGT.

This is a randomized prospective study comparing PEG vs NGT tube feeding in patients with acute dysphagic stroke. It assesses mortality, nutritional state, and treatment failure (primary outcome). Meets all selection criteria.
This is a review article about nutrition therapy for children with intestinal failure. Population is pediatric, not adult, and does not compare PEG vs NGT for swallowing disturbances.
This is a study developing and validating a dysphagia assessment scale for Huntington's disease. Not an intervention trial comparing PEG vs NGT.
This is a systematic review that found no RCTs comparing enteral tube feeding vs oral feeding in ALS/MND. The review itself is not an eligible RCT.
This study focuses on hospital malnutrition prevalence and screening, not on comparing PEG vs NGT. No mention of PEG or NGT comparison. Not an RCT.
This is a review article ('PURPOSE OF REVIEW') discussing various enteral feeding methods. It does not present primary RCT data comparing PEG vs NGT.
This is an RCT comparing PEG vs operative gastrostomy (surgical), NOT PEG vs NGT. The comparison group is incorrect for this review protocol.
This is a clinical practice guideline document, not a primary research study or RCT. Guidelines synthesize evidence but are not eligible for inclusion.
This is a review article aimed at primary care physicians discussing dysphagia management. It does not present RCT data comparing PEG vs NGT.
This is a retrospective comparative study comparing FPG, PEG, and SEG (different gastrostomy methods). It does not compare PEG vs NGT and is not an RCT.
This is a systematic review/meta-analysis that includes RCTs comparing PEG vs NGT, but the study itself is not a primary RCT. Systematic reviews are not eligible for inclusion in this review.

This is a prospective cohort study comparing PEG vs NGT, but it is NOT a randomised controlled trial. The authors explicitly state 'A randomized controlled study is needed'. Study design does not meet inclusion criteria.
This is a retrospective study comparing PEG vs no PEG (with functional therapy). It is not an RCT and the comparison is not PEG vs NGT.
This is a population-based registry study on ALS patients receiving various interventions (NIV, IV, EN). It does not compare PEG vs NGT and is not an RCT.
This is a methodological guidance document about reporting standards for RCTs. It is not a primary research study.
This study evaluates organoleptic characteristics of oral nutritional supplements (SON). It does not involve PEG vs NGT comparison and is not an RCT.
This is a meta-analysis comparing gastric vs post-pyloric feeding locations, not PEG vs NGT. Wrong intervention comparison and not a primary RCT.
This is a cross-sectional study examining nutritional status and length of hospital stay. It does not compare PEG vs NGT and is not an RCT.
This is a general review article about enteral nutrition. It does not present RCT data comparing PEG vs NGT.
This is a review article about PEG indications, technique, and nursing care. It does not present RCT data comparing PEG vs NGT.
This is a systematic review/meta-analysis comparing gastric vs post-pyloric feeding, not PEG vs NGT. Wrong comparison and not a primary RCT.
This is a case report about PVC-associated dysphagia. It does not compare PEG vs NGT and is not an RCT.

This is a retrospective review comparing PEG vs NGT in head and neck cancer patients. While it compares the right interventions, it is NOT a randomised controlled trial. Authors state 'A randomized prospective trial is needed'.
This is a descriptive analytic study about PEG acceptability and outcomes from patient/caregiver perspectives. It does not compare PEG vs NGT and is not an RCT.

This is an RCT in patients with dysphagia after stroke, but it compares two NGT securing methods (looped NGT vs conventional adhesive dressing), NOT PEG vs NGT. The intervention comparison does not match the review question.
This is an RCT using NGT feeding, but it compares two different nutritional formulas (whey protein vs casein), NOT PEG vs NGT. The intervention comparison does not match the review question.

This is an RCT comparing PEG vs non-PEG (likely NGT), but the population is mechanically-ventilated patients with ventilator-associated pneumonia and gastroesophageal reflux, NOT adults with swallowing disturbances or dysphagia. The population does not match the review criteria.
This is a retrospective observational study, NOT a randomised controlled trial. It does not compare PEG vs NGT at all - it examines associations between nutritional status and clinical outcomes.
This is a quasi-experimental design, NOT a randomised controlled trial. It compares usual care vs an aspiration risk-reduction protocol, NOT PEG vs NGT.
This is a descriptive report of a new PEG technique, NOT a randomised controlled trial. There is no comparison group and no evaluation of PEG vs NGT.
